$about: Camouwolf's launch defaults: the value every launch starts from for each option below, with what it does and example values. Change one for yourself without editing the installed package: run `camouwolf defaults`, which copies this file to your user config directory (~/.config/camouwolf/defaults.json on Linux, ~/Library/Application Support/camouwolf/defaults.json on macOS, %LOCALAPPDATA%\camouwolf\camouwolf\defaults.json on Windows) and prints its path, then edit the "default" values there. CAMOUWOLF_DEFAULTS=<path> reads your file from another path instead. Your file may also use the short form {"telemetry": false}. An unknown option or a value of the wrong type in it is an error. A value passed to the launch call (Camouwolf(), NewBrowser(), launch_options(); launchOptions() in TypeScript, with the same option names) wins over both files.

headless.about: Run Chromium's own headless mode. For a headed browser on an invisible display on Linux, pass headless='virtual' (or 'virtual-gpu') in the launch call.

humanize.about: Move the mouse, type and scroll like a person (the myuri engine) for Playwright's input calls. The launch call also takes a per-channel dict with a seed.

passthrough.about: Launch with this machine's own fingerprint: no identity is drawn and nothing about the device is spoofed (user agent, screen, GPU, fonts, timezone and languages are the host's). Behaviour options (proxy, headless, humanize, addons, block_images) still apply. Cannot be combined with an option that sets the identity (os, locale, geoip, config, fingerprint, screen, window, fonts, ...).

telemetry.about: Anonymous proxy telemetry. What is collected: per anti-bot provider (Cloudflare, Cloudflare Turnstile, DataDome, Akamai, PerimeterX, Kasada, Imperva, AWS WAF, hCaptcha, reCAPTCHA, Arkose Labs, Queue-it, Shape (F5), ThreatMetrix, Google BotGuard), how many encounters ended in success, challenge, block or unknown; and the launch's launcher name, launcher version, browser version, whether it is Pro, whether it is cross-OS (an identity OS other than this machine's), whether it is passthrough, and the proxy provider's domain only ('none' without a proxy). What is never collected: URLs, sites, page content, cookies, IP addresses, the proxy's username, password, host or port, or any identifier of you or this machine. What it is used for: publishing the success rates of proxy providers against no proxy, by release, Pro or not, and cross-OS or not, on the Camoufox website. How to turn it off: set this to false, set CAMOUWOLF_TELEMETRY=0, or set DO_NOT_TRACK=1.

geoip.about: Place the identity where its IP address is: timezone, locale, geolocation and WebRTC address from the public IP (through the proxy when there is one). Needs the geoip extra. The launch call also takes an IP address string.

geoip_db.about: Which GeoIP database geoip looks the IP up in; null is the one `camouwolf set --geoip` selected.

locale.about: The identity's locale(s). The first is the UI and Intl locale; all of them are navigator.languages and Accept-Language. null takes it from geoip, or the host's.

os.about: Operating system of the identity: "windows", "macos", "linux", or a list to choose from. null is what this host can pass for (its own OS, and Windows on a Linux host).

proxy.about: Proxy for the whole browser, in Playwright's format. A socks5:// proxy may carry a username and password.

block_images.about: Block every image. A page can tell, so it warns.

block_webrtc.about: Keep WebRTC to TCP through the proxy, with no UDP at all.

block_webgl.about: Turn WebGL off. Few real browsers lack it, so it warns.

disable_coop.about: Ignore Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy headers, so a popup a COOP page opens keeps its opener. It warns.

instant_animations.about: Finish every finite CSS and Web Animation at once. A page reads the zero duration back, so it warns.

show_cursor.about: Show where automation clicks, as a ripple a page cannot read, in screenshots and a watched window.

canvas_noise.about: Perturb canvas readback with a per-identity seed. Stock Chrome does not, so it warns.

pin_cpu_cores.about: Pin the browser to as many cores as the identity reports, instead of reporting the host's count. Costs real CPU; does nothing on macOS.

allow_os_mismatch.about: Allow an identity on an OS this host cannot render as. Its fonts and graphics then disagree with its user agent.

allow_addon_new_tab.about: Let extensions open tabs and windows of their own.

browser.about: Which installed browser build to launch (`camouwolf list`); null is the active one.

debug.about: Print the config sent to the browser (proxy credentials masked) and have the browser log to stderr.

i_know_what_im_doing.about: Silence the launcher's warnings, and drop conflicting switches instead of refusing them.
